arxiv-2208-04078.title: Affective Learning Objectives for Communicative Visualizations
arxiv-2208-04078.creator: Elsie Lee-Robbins and Eytan Adar
arxiv-2208-04078.description: Abstract When designing communicative visualizations, we often focus on goals that seek to convey patterns, relations, or comparisons (cognitive learning objectives). We pay less attention to affective intents–those that seek to influence or leverage the audience’s opinions, attitudes, or values in some way.

arxiv-2306-10469.title: Transferring Neural Potentials For High Order Dependency Parsing
arxiv-2306-10469.creator: Farshad Noravesh
arxiv-2306-10469.description: Abstract High order dependency parsing leverages high order features such as siblings or grandchildren to improve state of the art accuracy of current first order dependency parsers. The present paper uses biaffine scores to provide an estimate of the arc scores and is then propagated into a graphical model. The inference inside the graphical model is solved using dual decomposition.

arxiv-2503-15520.title: Agent-S: LLM Agentic workflow to automate Standard Operating Procedures
arxiv-2503-15520.creator: Mandar Kulkarni
arxiv-2503-15520.description: Abstract AI agents using Large Language Models (LLMs) as foundations have shown promise in solving complex real-world tasks. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based agentic workflow for automating Standard Operating Procedures (SOP). For customer care operations, an SOP defines a logical step-by-step process for human agents to resolve customer issues.

arxiv-2508-01812.title: HeQ : a Large and Diverse Hebrew Reading Comprehension Benchmark
arxiv-2508-01812.creator: Amir DN Cohen Hilla Merhav Yoav Goldberg, Reut Tsarfaty
arxiv-2508-01812.description: Abstract Current benchmarks for Hebrew Natural Language Processing (NLP) focus mainly on morpho-syntactic tasks, neglecting the semantic dimension of language understanding. To bridge this gap, we set out to deliver a Hebrew Machine Reading Comprehension (MRC) dataset, where MRC is to be realized as extractive Question Answering.

europmc-pmc5004837.description: Microsatellites or Single Sequence Repeats (SSRs) are extensively employed in plant genetics studies, using both low and high throughput genotyping approaches. Motivated by the importance of these sequences over the last decades this review aims to address some theoretical...

forster-passage-to-india-1924.description: The Marabar Caves case breaks every certainty of empire.

pmc-10737642.title: EMOTION REGULATION SUCCESS IN A LABORATORY TASK IN YOUNG ADULTS AND COGNITIVELY DIVERSE OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10737642.creator: Claire Growney, Tammy English
pmc-10737642.description: Age is associated with declines in cognitive resources viewed as important for emotion regulation, and older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) are expected to experience difficulty with emotion regulation. The present study examines how providing support through emotion regulation instructions might contribute to improved emotional well-being using different indices of emotion regulation success.

pmc-11367413.title: Protocol for electrophysiological measurements of circadian changes in excitability in dentate granule cells from adult mice
pmc-11367413.creator: Jose Carlos Gonzalez, Haeun Lee, Linda Overstreet-Wadiche
pmc-11367413.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryMany types of neurons exhibit a daily rhythm of intrinsic excitability. Here, we present a protocol for assessing circadian regulation of dentate granule cell excitability using a mouse model for conditional knockout of the molecular clock protein BMAL1. We describe steps for obtaining healthy oblique horizontal slices that contain the hippocampus and measuring intrinsic excitability and synaptic potentials by combining whole-cell patch-clamp recordings and perforant-path electric stimulation.

pmc-11411556.title: The first complete chloroplast genome for the species-rich genus Anthemis (Asteraceae)
pmc-11411556.creator: Eleonora Manzo, Salvatore Tomasello
pmc-11411556.description: Anthemis L. 1753 is a species-rich genus of Asteraceae. It includes species of economic value as ornamental, edible and medicinal plants. We report here the complete chloroplast genome of Anthemis cretica subsp. calabrica (Arcang.) R. Fern. 1975, the first chloroplast genome of any Anthemis species. For the scope, we have used long reads obtained with Oxford Nanopore technology.

pmc-11420493.title: Adsorption of cadmium from wastewater with activated carbons derived from pig fur biowaste: A comparative study of in-situ and ex-situ activation routes
pmc-11420493.creator: Henry Oghenero Orugba, Jude Ebieladoh Sinebe, Jeremiah Lekwuwa Chukwuneke, Victor Ikenna Okoro, Chukwudi Louis Enyi, Okwuchukwu Innocent Ani
pmc-11420493.description: The environmental challenges associated with cadmium contamination in wastewater have necessitated the development of high-performing activated carbons (ACs) for effective wastewater treatment. Adsorption capacity depends on both the surface area and the adsorption-active functional groups developed on the adsorbent's surface during activation. Proper manipulation of key process variables using the appropriate activation route produces highly efficient and economically viable ACs.

pmc-11577425.title: Stable Porous Organic Cage Nanocapsules for pH-Responsive Anticancer Drug Delivery for Precise Tumor Therapy
pmc-11577425.creator: Yanping Deng, Zhenhong Du, Shunfu Du, Nan Li, Wenjing Wang, Kongzhao Su, Daqiang Yuan
pmc-11577425.description: The search for drug nanocarriers with stimuli-responsive properties and high payloads for targeted drug delivery and precision medicine is currently a focal point of biomedical research, but this endeavor still encounters various challenges. Herein, a porous organic cage (POC) is applied to paclitaxel (PTX) drug delivery for cancer therapy for the first time.

pmc-11585594.title: Design of a novel state-feedback robust sliding-mode controller for a hydraulic turbine governing system
pmc-11585594.creator: Fang Dao, Yidong Zou, Jing Qian, Yun Zeng
pmc-11585594.description: This paper presents a novel state-feedback robust sliding-mode controller (SFRSMC) based on a mixed H2/H∞ approach to enhance the control performance of hydraulic turbine governing systems (HTGS) with complex conduit systems under external load disturbances and control signal uncertainties. A state-space model incorporating the dynamic responses of the HTGS is developed.

pmc-12602023.title: The Dilemma of Delayed Replantation of an Avulsed Tooth—Case Presentation
pmc-12602023.creator: Mihaela Chirila, Ioana Suciu, Ecaterina Ionescu, Lucian Chirila, Dana Bodnar, Adriana Vasilache
pmc-12602023.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Dental avulsion is one of the most severe forms of dental trauma, often requiring urgent intervention. The prognosis of replantation depends heavily on the extraoral time and the storage conditions of the avulsed tooth. This study is aimed at presenting and analyzing a clinical case of delayed replantation of a maxillary central incisor in a prepubertal patient, highlighting the therapeutic decisions, challenges, and long-term outcomes. A 14-year-old patient suffered avulsion of two maxillary incisors during a sports accident.

pmc-12703276.title: Occupational exposures to inorganic dust are associated with emphysema: the SCAPIS cohort
pmc-12703276.creator: Mathias Holm, Linus Schioler, Anna Dahlman-Hoglund, Håkan Tinnerberg, Martin Andersson, Annelie Behndig, Anders Blomberg, Kerstin Cederlund, Jonas Eriksson Ström, Christer Janson, Åse Johnsson, Eva Lindberg, Anders Lindén, Stefan Ljunggren, Andrei Malinovschi, Anna-Carin Olin, Ida Pesonen, Magnus Sk
pmc-12703276.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectivesThere is a lack of knowledge about whether occupational exposures increase the risk of emphysema, especially in never-smokers. Our objective was to determine if occupational exposures are associated with emphysema and impaired diffusing capacity.MethodsIn the Swedish CArdioPulmonary bioImage Study (SCAPIS), persons from the general population aged 50–64 answered a questionnaire and underwent CT of the lung as well as assessment of the diffusing capacity of their lungs for carbon monoxide (DLCO), presented as DLCO<lower limit of normal (LLN).

pmc-12982303.title: Plant and soil transcriptomics reveal the consequences of bioaugmentation of co-contaminated soil with Pseudomonas qingdaonensis ZCR6 during bacteria-assisted phytoremediation
pmc-12982303.creator: Magdalena Pacwa-Płociniczak, Agata Daszkowska-Golec, Sara Gobetti, Aki Sinkkonen, Tomasz Płociniczak
pmc-12982303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Our study evaluated the bioaugmentation potential of the Pseudomonas qingdaonensis ZCR6 strain to support the phytoremediation of multicontaminated soil. This metal-resistant strain expresses several plant growth–promoting features and petroleum hydrocarbon degradative potential in biochemical tests. A microcosm experiment with maize (Zea mays) treated with a suspension of live or thermally inactivated ZCR6 cells was performed (representing a scenario of unsuccessful bioaugmentation).

pmc-13655431.title: Effects of d-allulose intake during exercise training on heart rate response to submaximal exercise in untrained young adults: a pilot study
pmc-13655431.creator: Takamasa Tsuzuki, Takako Yamada, Teruhiko Koike, Takashi Umeda, Takayuki Negishi
pmc-13655431.description: [Purpose] d-Allulose has been reported to enhance fat oxidation during acute aerobic exercise; however, its effects during exercise training in humans remain unclear. We investigated the effects of d-allulose intake during exercise training on physiological responses to submaximal exercise in untrained young adults.

pmc-13690450.title: Decline in dementia patients during the COVID-19 pandemic: A cohort study in Taiwan
pmc-13690450.creator: Meng-Ju Tsai, Yu-Ruei Lin, Yung-Shuan Lin, Chun-Yu Chen, Jong-Ling Fuh
pmc-13690450.description: Background:The cognitive consequences of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in patients with dementia remain uncertain. This study examined whether COVID-19 infection was associated with cognitive decline.Methods:From October 2020 to October 2022, COVID-19-naive patients with dementia were recruited from a hospital-based memory clinic in Taipei. During follow-up, patients who developed COVID-19 were classified as the infected group, while others served as controls.
